records.text: Norman Finkelstein said Israel had a government policy called 'mowing the lawn' in Gaza, under which the IDF randomly killed Palestinians to limit population growth.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Something that lives in my mind rent-free is Norman Finkelstein informing me that Israel had a literal and actual government policy known as mowing the lawn in Gaza, where the IDF would just at random begin shooting and killing Palestinians to ensure that the population didn't grow.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 44:48. 'Mowing the grass' is a documented Israeli strategy of periodic military action to degrade Hamas's capabilities and deterrence. Reliable descriptions do not define it as random shooting of Palestinians to limit population growth; that added explanation directly misstates the strategy.

sources.title: Breaking the cycle in Gaza - Brookings Institution
sources.relevance: Explains mowing the grass as periodic degradation of Hamas capabilities, not random killing to reduce the population.

records.text: Financial Times reporting, as summarized by an unnamed website read by Candace Owens, described one Project Aurora model offering $9,000 per person to relocate about 500,000 Palestinians and another offering $5,000 plus four years of subsidized housing and one year of food assistance.
records.speaker: Financial Times

appearances.snippet: Two primary models emerged. One proposed a voluntary departure plan. $9,000 in cash per person aimed at relocating around 500,000 Palestinians outside of the Gaza Strip. A second model lowered direct payments to $5,000 but added four years of subsidized housing and one year of food assistance.

verification.notes: The reporting describes one relocation package worth about $9,000 per person for more than 500,000 people. The $5,000 cash payment plus subsidized housing and food were components of that package, not a separate second model as the statement says.

sources.title: BCG modelled plan to relocate Palestinians from Gaza
sources.relevance: Reports one $9,000-per-person relocation package, not two distinct models.

sources.title: The plan to relocate Palestinians from Gaza
sources.relevance: Breaks the $9,000 package into $5,000 cash plus housing and food support, refuting the two-model description.

conveyance.original_source: Financial Times reporting via an unnamed website summary

records.text: The Gaza Humanitarian Foundation's distribution hubs became killing fields where starving Palestinians were led to slaughter as the Israel Defense Forces fired on them.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Okay, that's what that was all about. And this was, of course, backed and funded by Israel, but you might recall that it was then discovered these were effectively just killing fields. ... The videos are horrific. They are available online and you should watch them. You should understand what the IDF army does: starving Palestinians effectively being led to the slaughter as the IDF fires upon them. That was the scandal.

verification.notes: UN and independent reporting confirm repeated killings of Palestinians seeking aid near GHF distribution sites, including incidents involving Israeli military fire. The stronger wording that the hubs were designed as killing fields or deliberately led people to slaughter is not conclusively established and was disputed by the IDF.

sources.title: Gaza: Israeli military kills Palestinians seeking food aid
sources.relevance: UN reporting confirms deaths involving Israeli fire near militarized aid distribution points.

sources.title: How Gaza aid sites became deadly
sources.relevance: Independent reporting documents repeated shootings of aid seekers while also presenting IDF denials and explanations.

records.text: Kushner said Gaza's waterfront property could be valuable and that, from Israel's perspective, he would do his best to move the people out and then clean it up, while noting he did not think Israel had said they could not return.
records.speaker: Jared Kushner

appearances.snippet: And Gaza's waterfront property—it could be very valuable if people would focus on kind of building up livelihoods. You think about all the money that's gone into this tunnel network and into all the munitions—if that would have gone into education or innovation—what could have been done? And so I think that it's a little bit of an unfortunate situation there, but I think from Israel's perspective, I would do my best to move the people out and then clean it up. But I don't think that Israel has stated that they don't want the people to move back there afterwards.

verification.notes: The original Harvard interview and independent reporting confirm all material parts of the quotation: Kushner called Gaza's waterfront property potentially valuable, said he would move people out and clean it up from Israel's perspective, and added that he did not think Israel had said people could not return afterward.

sources.title: Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, praises 'very valuable' potential of Gaza's 'waterfront property'
sources.relevance: AP quotes the Harvard interview's waterfront-property and move-people-out language.

sources.title: Here's What Jared Kushner Said About Gaza's Waterfront Property
sources.relevance: Provides the fuller quotation including Kushner's statement that he did not think Israel barred later return.
